Chlorambucil is one of a number of drugs for which reports of benefit exist.1 1. Hoofnagle JH, et al. Randomized trial of chlorambucil for pri- mary biliary cirrhosis. Gastroenterology 1986; 91: 1327–34. Malignant neoplasms. Chlorambucil is used in the manage- ment of a number of haematological malignancies including chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (p.653), Hodgkin’s disease (p.655), indolent low-grade non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas (p.656), and Waldenström’s macroglobulinaemia (p.658). It was former- ly used in polycythaemia vera (p.654) but is now largely super- seded. Ocular disorders, non-malignant. Chlorambucil is one of the immunosuppressants that may be considered for patients with uveitis (p.1515) unresponsive to corticosteroids in tolerable doses.1-3 1. Mudun AB, et al. Short-term chlorambucil for refractory uveitis in Behcet’s disease. Ocul Immunol Inflamm 2001; 9: 219–29. 2. Miserocchi E, et al. Efficacy and safety of chlorambucil in in- tractable noninfectious uveitis. Ophthalmology 2002; 109: 137–42. 3. Goldstein DA, et al.
